history.summary: CSV DUPLICATE FLAG: this row, 'Ganesh Tok [Tadong]', is a DUPLICATE of dataset row 920 'Ganesh Tok [Gangtok]' (file 920.json) - both describe the same well-known Ganesh temple-cum-viewpoint. The CSV town 'Tadong' is doubly WRONG: the temple is NOT in Tadong; it is ~7 km from Gangtok on the Gangtok-Nathula road in Gangtok district. Documented here as its own JSON per the batch instructions, but the canonical record for this temple is 920.json ('ganesh-tok-gangtok'). Ganesh Tok is a viewpoint first and a temple second: the shrine itself is tiny (only one person can enter at a time) with a television tower adjacent. The original structure dates to local devotion in the early 1950s; a larger ornate mandir was inaugurated in 2005 per one travel review (weakly sourced - verify). The hillock complex has a cafeteria, souvenir stalls, Smriti Van saplings planted by visitors, and a prayer-flag-lined staircase. The Himalayan Zoological Park (Bulbuley) is across the road.

town: Gangtok (CSV town 'Tadong' is WRONG and this row duplicates seq 920 'Ganesh Tok [Gangtok]' - canonical record is 920.json)
town_description: Ganesh Tok sits at 6,500 ft (~1,980 m) on a hillock off the Gangtok-Nathula road, 7 km from Gangtok town, in Gangtok district. It offers panoramic views of Gangtok town, Raj Bhawan and - on clear mornings - the Kanchenjunga massif. The spot is a standard stop on Gangtok sightseeing circuits, often combined with Hanuman Tok and Tashi View Point.

travel.road: About 7 km from Gangtok on the Gangtok-Nathula road; reachable by taxi (verify).

visitor_information.best_time: October to April, early morning for the clearest Kanchenjunga views; the seasonal cafeteria operates in tourist months.
